name: Eswatini
headline: Eswatini: +4.9% growth in 2025, 3.1% inflation, debt 45% of GDP
sections: Eswatini is a $5.2 billion economy (2025), the world's 173rd-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +4.9% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $13K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 28.1% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 3.1% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 4.8% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 34.2% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 54.3% (2025).
Gross government debt is 45% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has risen from 38% in 2020. The general government balance is −7.8% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is +2.4% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 107% of GDP (2024), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 1.0% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 48% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 64.3 years (2024). Population: 1.3 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
